articles.title: ‘We did 10 takes of it!’ Kerr Smith on Dawson’s Creek and filming US TV’s first gay kiss
articles.summary: As he releases a memoir, the actor opens up about the late James Van Der Beek, the magic of the Creek, and facing homophobia for playing gay in the 90s. There are worse things to spend a couple of decades chasing than the feeling of being young, successful and surrounded by people who love you.
body: “I’ve spent the last 25 years of my career trying to re-create that experience,” Smith says of the WB teen drama, on which he played the sensitive jock Jack McPhee for five seasons. “I’ve been trying to measure up to it my entire career.”

Speaking on a Zoom call this October, Smith is now 53, gray-haired and hatted with a brisk demeanor, Smith revisits that pursuit in his new memoir, I Don’t Want to Wait: My Life on Dawson’s Creek. Part oral history and part personal reckoning, the book draws on conversations with former castmates and colleagues, including big-hitters like Katie Holmes, to revisit the series, the protests that followed Jack’s coming-out storyline, and an episode of homophobic harassment Smith had never previously discussed. Highly rhapsodic and wistful about his experience on Dawson’s Creek, Kerr fully embraces the nostalgia in the memoir.

articles.title: ‘Sadistic, forbidden pleasure’: why Gone Girl is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our ongoing series of writers highlighting their go-to comfort films is a reminder of the dark joys that can be found in David Fincher’s devilish thriller.
body: “W hen I think of my wife, I always think of the back of her head,” narrates Ben Affleck in the opening scene of Gone Girl, David Fincher’s 2014 adaptation of the bestselling thriller novel. “I picture cracking her lovely skull, unspooling her brains, trying to get answers to the primal questions of any marriage: What are you thinking? How are you feeling? What have we done to each other?”

From the outset, Gone Girl probably sounds like quite an odd choice for a feelgood movie. The film follows Nick (Affleck) and Amy Dunne (Rosamund Pike), whose once-picture-perfect marriage has become a humiliatingly predictable tale of resentment and infidelity – and when Amy suddenly disappears in suspicious circumstances, it only gets more disturbing. But I find myself being drawn to this film every year when the days start to shorten. There is a strange catharsis (and comfort) in watching a scorned woman get her revenge, one meticulously planned move at a time.

articles.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon review – Iranian teen refugee paints boldly imaginative self-portrait
articles.summary: Soraya Akhlaghi filmed her perilous flight from Iran and precarious new life over five years on her phone, reassembled here with yearning animations. The world feels like an overwhelmingly forlorn place in this striking refugee self-portrait, shot on smartphone by Soraya Akhlaghi over five years…
body: Soraya is hoping to join her mother, who left for Austria after the death of Soraya’s father when she was a child. She winds up back in the Iranian capital, with her violent husband. Of Afghan heritage, she watches the Taliban takeover on TV – and over-identifies with the stricken populace desperate to board a US plane. Gearing up for the next escape attempt, if she can dodge being beaten by her partner, the Turkish border police offer more of the same. Whatever the latest travail, she narrates it to camera in a numbed monologue.

Luckily, Soraya has art. A born creator, she channels her struggles and despair into florid, intense drawings that repeatedly feature four figures: the moon, to whom she expresses her longing; a fox, who gives advice; her proxy, the clown, an avatar of her inner strength; and the craggy demons of her fears, which she also moulds into physical sculptures. This pantheon spills out in the film into vaporous, yearning animations, giving full rein to the imaginative force hemmed in by her harsh reality.

articles.title: 100 Sunset review – elliptical, elusive drama dreamlike through Toronto’s tight-knit Tibetan community
articles.summary: Kunsang Kyirong’s debut feature fades like a vapour trail in a mood of disorientation and dislocation. Not much happens and very little is explained in this elliptical, elusive drama by Canadian-Tibetan film-maker Kunsang Kyirong.
body: Kunsel is shy to the point of wordlessness; she is also a compulsive thief, rifling through handbags and coat pockets, with a knack for pilfering her victims’ most precious belongings. One night she steals a camcorder, and the shaky footage she subsequently films provides an inkling into her interior life – there is the faintest flicker of voyeurism as she begins spying on her neighbours, filming from her window. In particular, her gaze rests on Passang (Sonam Choekyi), a woman only a couple of years older than herself, who recently moved into number 100 with her husband.

The two women become friends, travelling on the subway to the wintry countryside outside Toronto, and take an English language class together. Passang is older, more experienced, clued up. There follows a storyline that offers the potential for action and suspense, involving a suitcase stuffed with $200,000 in cash, the payout from an informal savings and lending scheme in the building. But in the end, the drama of the missing money, like the film itself, fades like a vapour trail in the sky – though its mood of disorientation and dislocation is perhaps a reflection of Kunsel’s state of mind.

articles.title: Donald Trump Says He Was ‘Kidding’ About Making Dana White His Press Secretary
articles.summary: President Donald Trump has said he was only kidding about appointing Ultimate Fighting Championship president and CEO Dana White as his next White House press secretary.
body: On Sunday, however, Trump said it was “just a little fun,” according to AP.

“I was kidding, but I think Dana likes the idea, and he is a very capable guy,” Trump said, speaking to the media in Florida before leaving for Washington D.C. White is due to visit Trump at the White House on Monday.

As Variety reported Saturday, it was always unclear just how serious Trump was about offering the job to the executive, but the speculation was the latest in recent news regarding potential press secretaries. Trump had been asked during an interview whether musician Nikki Minaj would be considered for the position, to which he responded: “That’s a good idea. I think I’ll have to think about that… I’m going to think about that.”

Zacharia served as Trump’s press secretary for just five days before she was let go — the shortest tenure in White House history. She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who held the position from Jan. 20, 2025 through Aug. 27. In October, she announced she joining Fox News Channel as a contributor. At 27, she was the youngest person in American history to hold the position.

articles.summary: Nicholas Denton (“Talamasca: The Secret Order,” “Dangerous Liaisons”) is attached to portray cult British horror filmmaker Michael Reeves opposite Tim Downie (“Baldur’s Gate 3,” “Outlander”) as Hollywood horror legend Vincent Price in “Tragedy Man: The Making of Michael Reeves.” Hugh Bonneville…
body: U.K.-based Sceadwe Films and CrossBorder Films have teamed to produce the project. Production is expected to begin in late November. CrossBorder Films will handle international sales and introduce the film to buyers at the American Film Market in Los Angeles.
Sceadwe Films is the U.K. genre production banner co-founded by producer and writer Justin Stanley, while CrossBorder Films is a London-based film production and sales company.

Set against 1960s London and the haunted countryside of East Anglia, “Tragedy Man” follows the young Reeves as he stakes his burgeoning career on “Witchfinder General.” His financiers bring in Hollywood horror star Price for the lead role, a casting choice Reeves vehemently opposes, seeing the veteran actor’s theatrical style as everything he wants to leave behind. Price, meanwhile, is confronting his own fears of becoming obsolete as Hollywood changes around him.

articles.title: Jeff Goldblum, John Turturro, Rian Johnson and More Set for Marrakech Film Festival Conversations
articles.summary: Hollywood stars Jeff Goldblum and John Turturro, and “Knives Out” director Rian Johnson are among those set to take part in the Conversations program during the 23rd edition of the Marrakech Film Festival, which runs Nov. 20-28.
body: The festival commented that the Conversations would “offer a comprehensive overview of the sensibilities that are shaping contemporary cinema. Whether in major Hollywood productions or deeply personal works, genre films or intimate narratives, their experiences reveal a wide range of approaches to depicting the world, examining society and moving audiences.”
In a separate announcement on Monday, the festival said that it would honor Goldblum, Turturro and Moroccan actor Younès Mégri during the event.

Goldblum, whose credits range from David Cronenberg’s “The Fly” to Jon M. Chu’s “Wicked,” said, “It is beyond a thrill and a privilege to be honored at the iconic Marrakech International Film Festival. What a captivating place! This glorious city with such deep roots in storytelling and craftsmanship! I feel wildly lucky indeed. It is truly a rapturous joy—and an adventure upon which I can’t wait to embark.”

articles.title: Anthony Chen-Produced ‘Somewhere in the South’ Wins Top Prize at Taiwan Creative Content Fest Pitching Awards, ‘Reunion Dinner’ Takes Three
articles.summary: “Somewhere in the South,” a Malaysian feature written and directed by Tan Ce Ding and produced by Anthony Chen, the Singaporean director of Cannes Caméra d’Or winner “Ilo Ilo,” won the $35,000 TAICCA × CNC Feature Film Grand Award at the 2026 Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) pitching awards in…
body: Set in a forgotten town in southern Malaysia, “Somewhere in the South” follows 25-year-old Boon, who helps his mother run their struggling temple. When a by-election brings his charismatic childhood friend JC back to town to lead a campaign, Boon is hired as JC’s driver and reluctantly becomes the party’s tiger mascot. Then the mascot is stolen, and his fragile sense of identity is thrown into question.

“Reunion Dinner,” from Make A Deal International Production, led the awards with three wins: the Videoland Ingenuity Award, MPA Asia Pacific Grand Award and the award from NAFF, the Network of Asian Fantastic Films project market at South Korea’s Bucheon festival.

Several other projects received two awards each. “Saving Tuvalu,” produced by Media Stockade and Filmtank, won the Hakka Public Communication Foundation Confluence Award and Taiwan Mobile: Content Power Award. Critical Hits Production’s “Turns Out It’s Not BL But BFF” received the 2026 TCCF MyPick Project Award and Kaohsiung Film Archive’s KFA Original Award. Mirror Entertainment’s “Romance in Hell” won the Hami Video Creativity Award and udnFunLife IP Potential Award.

articles.title: Find out who's in the running for this year's Booker Prize
articles.summary: The winner of this year's literary award will be announced in London on Monday.
body: Past Booker Prize winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart are among the contenders to scoop the prestigious literary award this year, after a shortlist selection process that the judges described as "a tussle".
Jamaican writer James is nominated this year for his latest novel The Disappearers; while Scottish author Stuart is shortlisted for John of John.
This year's other contenders are award-winning US novelist Elizabeth Strout, and British authors M John Harrison, Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry.
But seven books that appeared on the longlist in July were jettisoned, and Dame Mary Beard, who chaired the judging panel, said agreeing on the final six "has been, to put it mildly, hard work".

articles.title: Mariah Carey set to headline 2027 music festival
articles.summary: She is due to perform at Powderham Castle near Exeter in June 2027 with the Sugababes and Eternal.
body: Best-selling female solo artist Mariah Carey has been announced as the third headliner for a music festival.

Live at Powderham organisers said the singer would bring her Firefly summer tour to Powderham Castle in Devon on 27 June 2027, alongside special guests Sugababes, with additional support from R&B group Eternal.
The All I Want For Christmas Is You and Love Takes Time singer has amassed more than 19 Billboard Hot 100 Number One singles – more than any solo artist in history.
She is due to be headlining the festival near Exeter alongside Shania Twain, who has been set to perform on 24 June 2027; and Alex Warren, performing on 26 June.

articles.title: Ink Review: Danny Boyle's Tabloid Media Origin Story Will Make You Feel Sick
articles.summary: Modern tabloid journalism gets the uncomfortable, sickening origin story it deserves in Danny Boyle's Ink. Here's our review.
body: Journalism and media have undergone significant changes in the 21st century. The internet has altered everything and barriers are gone. The gatekeepers who used to be there to say what was or wasn't news don't exist, at least not in the way they used to. Director Danny Boyle has examined this "Give 'em what they want" tabloid media culture in his latest movie "Ink," which will make anyone who values real journalism sick to their stomach.

Adapting the play of the same name, the movie traces the origins of the British gossip rag The Sun, focusing on a group of misfit visionaries who had an idea for a new kind of news. Rather than simply report "the news," why not give people what they want instead?
points: Modern tabloid journalism gets the uncomfortable, sickening origin story it deserves in Danny Boyle's Ink.
